teams.heading: Tadhg Furlong cleared to play as Ireland prepare for Fiji
teams.body: Tadhg Furlong has been cleared to play after avoiding a ban, following what the Disciplinary Committee called a 'unanimous' decision over an alleged testicle grab. Ireland's 'A' squad are also set to face Fiji, while Jake White's men face Ireland in the November block alongside France and Italy. Fiji come into that block off a 34-28 win over Japan.

lead.why: It is the only shortlist item not already covered, and its Disciplinary Committee outcome bears on Fiji's November opponent Ireland.

teams.heading: Argentina name Bernasconi-led XV for uncapped clash with England A
teams.body: England A host Argentina XV at Bath this Friday in an uncapped match, and the visitors have named a 27-man squad headlined by hooker Bernardo Bernasconi of Benetton. Coach Álvaro Galindo, a former Puma, has picked several Europe-based players, including Pedro Delgado of Harlequins and Bristol Bears back row Benjamín Grondona, who has five caps. The fixture gives players from both sides a chance to push for call-ups to the test arena, and both England and Argentina play four capped tests in the November Internationals.

lead.why: It is the only new national-team item in the shortlist; the two Bristol–Leicester stories and the USA win are either already covered or women's rugby.

teams.heading: Ireland face Argentina without Gallo, Carreras and Oviedo after squad naming
teams.body: Ireland's next opponents have named a 33-man squad for Dublin, and it comes without several players. Facundo Isa returns in place of the injured Santiago Grondona, having missed international duty in 2024 and 2026. Thomas Gallo and Santiago Carreras were named before being ruled out with injuries, and Gallo, Carreras and Joaquín Oviedo are out long-term. Ignacio Ruiz is also unavailable.

lead.why: It is the newest national-team item in the pack, and it sets out who Ireland will face in Dublin, with Argentina's injury list and Facundo Isa's return.

teams.heading: Valorugby Emilia beat Fiamme Oro 38-31 in Coppa Italia Girone 2
teams.body: Domestic rugby rather than the Azzurri takes the spotlight here, with Valorugby Emilia winning 38-31 at Fiamme Oro in Rome on Saturday in the Coppa Italia's Girone 2. Valorugby led 28-17 at the break before Fiamme Oro cut the gap late on. Valorugby's Hugo kicked six from six, and the win puts them top of Girone 2 on 20 points, ahead of Fiamme Oro on 17. Viadana also won their early fixture, 22-10 against Accademia Nazionale Ivan Francescato.

lead.why: The only fresh item in the pack that isn't already in the reader's feed; the new U18 result has already been reported today.

teams.heading: Finn Russell opens up on bid to make history against All Blacks
teams.body: Finn Russell's Daily Mail interview turns to Scotland's bid to make history against the All Blacks. New Zealand have won 31 of the 33 previous meetings, with draws in 1964 and 1983, and Scotland have never beaten them. Saturday's Murrayfield match is the 34th between the sides. Scotland host Australia and Japan at Murrayfield after that, before the Finals Weekend at Twickenham.

lead.why: It is the freshest national-team item in the pack, and it concerns Scotland's stake in the All Blacks match.

teams.heading: Wales open November against Japan, then face the All Blacks and Wallabies
teams.body: Wales open their three-Test November against Japan at Principality Stadium, then host New Zealand and Australia, before the Nations Championship Finals Weekend at Twickenham from 27 to 29 November. Japan arrive after a mixed run: Eddie Jones' side beat Italy 27-10 in their opener but lost 36-20 to Ireland and 42-15 to France, then fell 34-28 to Fiji in Tokyo on 24 October. The 2025 meeting in Cardiff went Wales' way 24-23.

lead.why: The only national-team item in the pack with substantive detail; the other national-team items are a women's squad story and an already-reported Scarlets piece, and the rest are club or stale.

teams.heading: Santiago Carreras and Thomas Gallo ruled out injured; Chocobares awaits HIA
teams.body: Argentina lost two first-choice men to injury on the eve of their London camp, with Santiago Carreras (Bath) and Thomas Gallo (Lyon) ruled out and replaced by Mateo Soler (Dogos) and Rodrigo Martínez (Dragons). Centre Chocobares (Toulouse) was awaiting the outcome of a head injury assessment at the time, with Matías Moroni (Bristol Bears) placed on stand-by. Carreras and Gallo are now listed among the long-term absentees, and Moroni is not in the Ireland squad.

lead.why: The Ireland and England A rosters have already been reported, so this is the strongest genuinely new item: two first-choice backs lost to injury and a centre awaiting a head injury assessment.

teams.heading: Back in January, Roar column said Wallabies were stuck in second tier
teams.body: A January opinion piece on The Roar argued the Wallabies are 'well and truly stuck in second tier of teams' as Australia prepare to host the 2027 World Cup. Its author asked whether there are actually 24 teams 'worthy' of playing at a World Cup, and whether rugby is stretching its resources too thin. The piece set that expansion against football's 32-team finals.

teams.heading: Dave Rennie leaves Tuipulotu and Darry out of northern tour squad
teams.body: Dave Rennie has left Patrick Tuipulotu and Sam Darry out of the 36-man squad for the northern leg, with Crusaders lock Jamie Hannah leapfrogging both. Stephen Donald, on The Aftermatch with Kirst and Beav, said Tuipulotu is "hugely unlucky", and named Darry as another lock who deserved a place. Rennie also left out Du'Plessis Kirifi and Kyren Taumoefolau, while Ruben Love, Ardie Savea, Samisoni Taukei'aho, Shannon Frizell and Luke Jacobson are sidelined for the end-of-year matches.

lead.why: A squad story about who missed the 36-man northern tour squad, which is not covered by the earlier Fainga'anuku, Kirwan or Mo'unga editions.

teams.heading: Hansen says Erasmus is resting Etzebeth, Pollard for World Cup
teams.body: Steve Hansen believes Rassie Erasmus is using the November internationals to rest key players before the World Cup. Cheslin Kolbe, Eben Etzebeth, Andre Esterhuizen and Handré Pollard are all missing from the touring squad through injury, but Hansen thinks Erasmus is also giving some players a breather. "There's no doubt about that with Etzebeth," he said on the Rugby Unity podcast. Hansen expects Erasmus to back his regular starters when it matters, though the touring party includes six uncapped players.

lead.why: It is a new national-team story about the Springboks' squad, and the shortlist's other new items are either the Furlong story already reported or Stormers and Bulls match coverage.
